nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A notice has appeared on the board in the Guild Hall of Steady Steps. It is written in Maple's neatest hand, signed by everyone, and pinned with a very firm pin.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'Be it known that the Guildmaster is to take a day off. The day may be spread across several days, at his leisure, which he is also to take.'

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A vote! Behind my back! I am the guildmaster! I invented votes!

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You voted too. You voted against yourself, asked for a recount, and then voted against yourself again.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: We like you a great deal, Chad. That's the whole reason. You haven't sat down since the Comet.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I've never seen him not busy. I didn't know it was something you could be allowed to stop.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I once read that a person who cannot sit down has often forgotten what it feels like to stand still on purpose. I wrote it in the margin of item forty. It has aged very well.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I am extremely rested already. Observe. I could run this hall in my sleep. I have, on several occasions.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: That is not the argument you think it is.

nodes.prompt: How do you vote on Chad's day off?

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: That makes it unanimous again. We've voted unanimously eleven times this week. It's become a habit.

options.label: Yes, and I will help run the hall.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Help accepted. I have a list. It has one item on it that says 'let the hall be'.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A principled position. Snacks are the foundation of every great decision I have ever witnessed.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...Fine. A day off. I will take it extremely seriously. I will be the best at it that anyone has ever been.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Resting is not a contest, Chad.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Everything is a contest if you are brave enough. Where do I begin? Is there a form?

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I think you just sit. And, maybe, see what happens.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Sit. And see what happens. Right. That sounds terrifying. I will do it at once.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Chad arrives at breakfast with a roll of paper that unrolls across the whole table and a little way down the hall.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: The Schedule of Rest. It is a masterpiece. Six o'clock: Sit. A quarter past: Sit Differently. Half past: Look Out of a Window Thoughtfully. A quarter to seven: Lie Down (Briefly).

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: There's a column for 'Rest Achieved', Chad. It's got a tick box.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Rest is training. I have always said so. So it must be trained! With rigour! In fifteen-minute blocks!

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Rest that has a timetable is just work in slippers.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: What happens if you finish a block early? Do you, can you rest harder?

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Excellent question. There is a bonus section. It is called Extra Rest.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit, who has been lying beside the hearth for some hours with his chin on the floor and his eyes half shut, lets out a long sigh. It is, without question, the most competent rest anyone in the hall has done all week.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Look at him. He does not have a schedule. He has not looked at a clock. He has simply stopped.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: He is a professional. He has been practising since a puppy.

nodes.prompt: What do you do with the Schedule of Rest?

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: A boat! Brilliant. Now it's a thing you can float, and nobody has to tick anything.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Oh, that is a brave pen stroke. Cross out another and we shall have started something.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Thank you. I shall file it under 'things Chad made when he was nervous', which is a large cabinet.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Without the schedule I do not know what time it is. Or what I am supposed to feel. Or when it is allowed to stop.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: That is the point, Chad. You are not supposed to know. At your own pace. Whatever that turns out to be.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: You could start by sitting next to Biscuit. He's very good at it, and he doesn't mind teaching.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Chad lowers himself to the floor, with the care of a man entering a cold lake, and lies beside the dog. For almost nine seconds nothing happens. Then Biscuit moves his tail, once, in welcome.

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: Woof.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Behind the hall there is a garden that nobody has used for years, and in it, between two trees, somebody has hung a hammock. It is the colour of a tangerine. It is, Pip says, the most welcoming thing she has ever built.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I made it on my day off. I'd never had one. It took me two hours and I didn't mind a minute of it.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: A hammock! Excellent. A well-designed rest device. I shall enter it in the correct manner.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: He climbs in. He is, throughout, sitting perfectly upright, with his hands on his knees, like a man waiting to be interviewed by a hammock.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Chad. You can lie back. It holds you. That's what it's for.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I am lying back. This is how I lie back. Observe the angle.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A small sound comes from the hedge. A goat steps out, a cream-coloured one, with small horns and a calm eye, chewing on what turns out, on inspection, to be a corner of the Schedule of Rest.

nodes.speaker: goat
nodes.text: Meh.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It's the goat from Brun's door! The one that was the first knock in eleven years. It must have walked all the way up the stair.

nodes.speaker: goat
nodes.text: Mm. The sun is warm. That is the whole plan.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The goat lies down on the warm grass, folds its legs under itself, and closes its eyes. It does this without effort, without a diagram, and without once checking whether it is doing it right.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: It has no schedule. It has eaten my schedule. I am not sure whether to be offended or inspired.

nodes.prompt: How do you help Chad into the hammock?

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: There. It's steady. It's not going anywhere. You can let go of the sides, and let it have you.

options.label: Get in first, to show him.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Move over. Okay. See? You just let your head be heavy. That's, honestly, all it is.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: It's allowed. Nobody needs you for a bit. That is the nicest sentence I know, so I thought I'd say it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Slowly, one muscle at a time, as if somebody were turning down a very loud radio, Chad lies back. The hammock sways. He looks up through the leaves. His face does something nobody has seen it do before: nothing at all.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Oh. It is quiet up here. Has it always been this quiet?

nodes.speaker: goat
nodes.text: Meh.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Word has gone out along the roads that the guildmaster is learning to stop. By afternoon the garden has visitors, each with a small bag and the look of somebody asked to give a lesson in something they never thought of as a skill.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I brought soup. I hold the bowl in both hands, and I do not do anything else until it is empty. That is the whole of my method. It is a very good method.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: I stop at every landing, even where there is no stair. A landing is just a place that says, you may stand here for a moment. They are everywhere, once you start to see them.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I go to bed when the sun does, and I sleep eleven hours. It sounds like nothing. It is the bravest thing I have ever done. I was very frightened of it.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: I do not rest. I go slowly. It is, I find, the same thing from the inside.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Four ways! Four masters! I will master all of them by teatime.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: You will not. And that is the first lesson. You are not supposed to be good at it.

nodes.prompt: Whose way of resting do you try first?

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: Both hands. Warm bowl. Nothing else. There. Do you feel the little pause before the first spoonful? That is the rest.

reply.speaker: tamsin
reply.text: You have found one already. You are standing in it. Take a breath, and let your shoulders arrive.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: Lovely. Tonight, sundown. I will bring a lantern that does not quite go out, and I will sit beside you until you are asleep, if you like.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: This is difficult. Each of them is very good at it, and I seem to be very good at the wrong end of it.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: Nobody is good at rest. We are only practised at letting it happen.

nodes.speaker: tamsin
nodes.text: And nothing here has a deadline. Not even this. You may start again as often as you need to, and begin where you are.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Chad sits down on the grass between a yeti with a bowl, a Weatherkeeper at an invisible landing, a lighthouse keeper on the verge of a nap, and a tortoise who has not moved in some time.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: He does his best. It is a very small, very honest best. It is, everyone agrees, the best they have seen him do.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: On the fourth day of the day off, forty-one crates arrive at the hall's front step at once. They are Brun's. They are all hammers. They are accompanied by a goose, who has opinions, and a note saying 'Sorry, early. B.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Right. Forty-one crates. Pip, the east wall. Juno, the tally book. Bertram, the goose.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I shall engage the goose in conversation. It is, historically, the only thing that works.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I've counted them. It's forty-one, I'm sure, and one of them is a hat.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Stack them by size, hats at the front. And please, mind the Duck Mat.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the upstairs window, in a hammock he has carried in under his arm, Chad is trying very hard to lie still. He fails. His whole body leans towards the stairs.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I can see it from here. The crates are the wrong way round. The goose is winning. I am going down. I am only going to supervise from a little distance. From inside the crates.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Chad. You have a day off.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I know! I am having it! I am simply having it near the crates!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Below, without him, the guild does it. Not perfectly, and not quickly. A crate goes in the wrong place and is moved. Bertram negotiates a ceasefire with the goose. Juno finds the hat. Somebody laughs.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: By the end of the afternoon the whole hall is orderly, in a gently lopsided way, and nobody has raised their voice.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: It is fine. It is all fine. They have done it perfectly well without me, and I am so relieved, and a very small part of me wants to lie down and cry.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Chad at the window?

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: They have. They have got it, and it is theirs. I think I have been holding it very tightly for a very long time.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: Yes. Yes, I will. I will sit down at the window and watch my hall be a good hall without me. Move over.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: It does. That is what a good hall looks like when the person who built it is not standing in the middle of it.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: A hall that runs without you is the best thing you ever built, Chad. Rest is training, and this is what it was for.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...Maple. May I say I am proud of all of you? From a safe, seated distance?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: You may. It is allowed.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Evening. The others have gone in for supper and the garden has gone gold and quiet. Chad is in the hammock, not upright at all, with one arm hanging down and the goat asleep underneath.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: Can I sit with you? I won't say anything. I'm just bringing the cup.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Please. And Maple, I can hear you pretending to look at a flowerpot. Come and sit.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: It was a very interesting flowerpot.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I want to tell you why I do not stop. I have not told anyone. I started at Level 1, like everyone, and I was very small, and I thought: if I keep moving, nobody will notice I do not know what I am doing.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: And then I became the guildmaster, and everyone was looking at me, and I thought: I must not stop. If I stop, they will see that under the cape it is just me.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: I thought that too. When I first knocked. I thought, I need to be doing something, so they don't see I'm not sure I belong.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Chad. I lit the first fire, you will remember. I have watched you for a great many years from beside it. It is just you under the cape. That is the part everybody came for.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: ...It is?

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: It always was. The cape is a very good cape. It is not the reason.

options.label: You are enough when you are still.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: When I am still. I did not know that was a thing a person could be told. Thank you. I think I will need to hear it again tomorrow.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: You can hear it every day. I'll say it. I'm quite good at remembering things.

options.label: We like you with the cape off, too.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: With it off. Even the cape. I shall consider it. Possibly I shall hang it on a hook, as an experiment.

options.label: Rest is part of the story.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: It is the longest part of any story that lasts. We just tend to skip it when we tell it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The goat opens one eye, checks that everything is as it should be, and closes it again. The hammock sways. Somewhere in the hall a kettle begins to sing.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I think I can hear the garden. It has been going on this whole time. I did not know it was so busy.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It has been decided, by a vote nobody can quite remember holding, that the day off will end with a Great Do Nothing, to which everyone is invited, at which nothing at all will happen, and for which, it turns out, a great deal of preparation is required.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have a list. It is, I think, my finest. 'Item one: nothing, planned in detail.' It has seventeen sub-items. Sub-item nine is 'a place to put the nothing'.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I've done blankets. There are forty blankets. They don't match, and I think that's the best bit.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: And I've asked people to come with no plans. It's harder than it sounds. Everybody keeps asking what to bring.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I have planned nothing so thoroughly that I am a little worried it will go wrong. I have a whole section on what to do if there is nothing happening and it becomes awkward.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: That is 'what to do if there is nothing happening'. It's just the Nothing. It's working.

nodes.speaker: goat
nodes.text: Meh.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The goat, who has no list and no blanket, is lying in the exact middle of the lawn. It is generally agreed that this is the best place for the Nothing to be, and that the goat found it first.

nodes.prompt: What do you bring to the Nothing?

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: A blanket. That's the lot. It's perfect. It's the whole of what anyone needs.

options.label: A book I do not plan to read.

reply.speaker: bertram
reply.text: A book not to be read. A beautiful object. It is the finest kind of luggage, and it never weighs anything.

options.label: A friend who is also busy.

reply.speaker: juno
reply.text: That's the best thing you could bring. Busy people are the ones who need the Nothing most.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: It is a curious thing. I have spent my life collecting items to do. I find that I am happier than I have ever been collecting an item to simply be.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: At your own pace, everyone. That is the only rule. I have written it on a stick. It is the only thing I have written in a month that I did not need to revise.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: One by one the lanterns are hung, and the garden softens in the dusk. Forty blankets lie ready on the grass, like a very large, very untidy flag of a country where nobody has to be anywhere.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It begins, as these things do, with nobody saying that it has begun. People arrive. They find a blanket. They lie down on it. That is all that happens, and it takes about an hour, and nobody wants it to end.

nodes.speaker: hush
nodes.text: I have brought soup, and I have not served it. It is simply there. I find it is a great comfort to have soup near nothing.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: It is the most punctual thing I have ever attended. It has begun exactly when it began.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I have not checked the list once. I am a little frightened. It is wonderful.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I had prepared a speech. It has a goose in it. I am not going to give it. I find I am, for the first time, completely content to be one person on a blanket among many.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The whole guild lies on its back in the long gold light. Somewhere a moth, which has followed the story all the way from the Isles, settles on a drum. The goat sighs. The hammock sways. Nobody says anything useful, and the silence is full of it.

nodes.prompt: What do you do with your nothing?

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: A cloud is a very good teacher. It goes where it goes, and it is never once in a hurry.

reply.speaker: hush
reply.text: Yes. Eyes closed. The best of all the ways. You may as well take the whole afternoon.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Oh, that is the loveliest. All of us, in and out, a little out of step, and none of us minding.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: When the lanterns have burned low they carry the blankets in, and the hall is just as they left it: standing, warm, a little untidy, with the small red line in the hearth, exactly where it always is.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The hall is still standing. It was standing the entire time. I want that written down in a very large hand.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Everything held. The fire, the roof, the goose. It held without me, and it held with me lying down, and I could not be prouder of any of it.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: You said you didn't know what to do with a day off. What did you do?

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I think I let it do me. It turned out to be the one thing I had never tried.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: You told someone once to look up sometimes. I looked up the whole way here. It made all of it a bit softer.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: You told someone once to go at their own pace. I've been doing it. I'm a lot slower than I thought, and a lot further on.

nodes.speaker: juno
nodes.text: You told someone once that they don't have to be good at it yet. I'm not. I'm just here. It's wonderful.

nodes.speaker: bertram
nodes.text: I have a new item. Item one hundred and thirteen. 'Do nothing, regularly, with friends.' I have not ticked it. I do not think it is the kind of item that has a tick.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like, rest when you need to, and when you need to, rest properly, on purpose. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would, and have a lie-down in the middle of it. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day, and be curious about stopping, too. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Far away a bell rings, a lamp winks, a chime sings, a table is laid, a small fire is kept and a comet makes its slow way home.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And in a hall on a hill, nothing at all happens, at its own pace, with a goat on the rug and a guildmaster fast asleep in a chair he did not once check was the right one.
